cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! Eighty years of the Meridian this autumn. The Board has approved a Jubilee at the summit. At our summit. I have plans. I have had plans for twenty years. How large shall we dream?

left.label: As large as the Company will pay for
left.outcome: "Magnificent! The Company will pay for a great deal. Eventually."

right.label: Modestly; the water is low
right.outcome: "Modest. Yes. A modest Jubilee. Those words have never met."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The guest list. Commissioner Kell, naturally. Both shore inspectors. The reeve, if she will come, which she will not. And the Board asks whether the boat-clans should be 'visible'. Their word.

left.label: Visible; invite Bram
left.outcome: Bram accepts by not refusing. Pell is nervous and pretends otherwise.

right.label: Not visible
right.outcome: "Sensible. The Board prefers a tidy summit." The Reach hears anyway.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Board would like a 'demonstration of throughput' at the Jubilee. Forty vessels in a day, before the Commissioner's eyes. Forty. Keeper, I have promised them fifty.

left.label: Fifty, then
left.outcome: "Magnificent! I knew it. I said so. I said the Keeper would say fifty."

right.label: Forty, and none aground
right.outcome: "Forty. Well. I shall tell them fifty and hope they cannot count."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Pell wants bunting money. I want spindle money. There's one chest. Sorry. If the bunting goes up and the spindle goes, the Commissioner will see fifty boats and one of them will be stuck in the chamber.

left.label: Spindles first
left.outcome: "Thank you. Sorry. Thank you." Pell learns of it and is wounded for a week.

right.label: Bunting; the spindle will hold
right.outcome: "It might. Roughly. I'll pray." She does not pray. She oils it, nightly.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The Board's Jubilee speech is here for checking. It thanks 'the Ninefold Reservoirs, whose bounty feeds the summit'. I can't sign that. Sorry. I can't. Someone has to. It doesn't have to be me.

left.label: Strike the line
left.outcome: The speech thanks 'the water'. Ardent notices the change and asks who made it.

right.label: Sign it yourself
right.outcome: You sign for the reservoirs. Quenn looks at the signature and says nothing at all.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: For the demonstration day I'll need the pound a mark higher than it is. The only way is to close the gate for three days before and let it fill. Pell says three days of no boats before a Jubilee is 'a bad look'.

left.label: Close for three days
left.outcome: The pound fills. The queue grumbles. On the day, every boat floats.

right.label: Run it as it is
right.outcome: "Roughly. Yes. Roughly it'll float them." She does not sound sure.

cards.speaker: kell
cards.text: Commissioner Kell, a week early, unannounced. The Board's view is that rehearsed Jubilees are Jubilees for the Board and unrehearsed ones are for the truth. I am here for the truth. Do carry on.

left.label: Carry on exactly as usual
left.outcome: He watches the gate for a week. He writes very little. He sees everything.

right.label: Rehearse anyway, openly
right.outcome: "Refreshingly honest. Regrettably, so is the rehearsal." A barge grounds during it.

cards.speaker: kell
cards.text: A private word. The Board's Jubilee has a second purpose. It wishes to be seen at the summit before certain 'structural matters' become public. Regrettably, I cannot say more. I can say that your cooperation will be remembered.

left.label: You have it
left.outcome: "Excellent." He does not say what for. You will find out.

right.label: What structural matters?
right.outcome: "The Board's view is that you do not need to know. My view is that you already do."

cards.speaker: kell
cards.text: The Commissioner has reviewed the demonstration plan and has one amendment. The boat-clans' moorings are 'in the sightline'. The Board would prefer the Reach empty for the day. Only the day. Regrettably firm.

left.label: Ask the Reach to move for a day
left.outcome: Bram moves the Reach down the pound without a word. The word comes later.

right.label: The Reach stays in the sightline
right.outcome: "Regrettably noted." Kell does not mention it again. The Board does.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The day, Keeper! Bunting, band, both inspectors in their best, the Commissioner on the dais, and forty vessels queued to the horizon. Give the word. Give it magnificently.

left.label: Open the gate
left.outcome: The first barge rises to applause. The band plays something that is nearly a tune.

right.label: A word first: thank the hands
right.outcome: You thank the hands before the Board. Pell winces. Dace does not know where to look. The town roars.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Thirty-one vessels and the west paddle has stopped. Stopped, Keeper, before the Commissioner. Quenn is inside the gear. She says a quarter hour. The Board is looking at its watches.

text_variants.text: Thirty-one vessels and the west paddle is singing. New spindle. Quenn's spindle. The Commissioner has asked who maintains the gear. I would like to say I do. I shall say she does.

left.label: Give Quenn her quarter hour
left.outcome: Fourteen minutes. The paddle runs. The Board applauds the engineer, which has never happened.

right.label: Run the east paddle alone; press on
right.outcome: Slow passages, one gate. Forty-two by dusk. The Board did not notice the paddle. Quenn did.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Commissioner will speak at dusk. Then the Keeper. Then me, magnificently briefly. The Commissioner's speech thanks the reservoirs. Yours is your own. I am asking, as a friend, that it not mention the gauge.

left.label: Don't mention the gauge
left.outcome: You thank the town, the hands, the water. Kell nods. Pell breathes.

right.label: Mention the gauge
right.outcome: You say the pound has fallen a mark a watch since you came. The band stops. Kell does not move. Quenn, in the crowd, weeps.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The town's picking bunting out of the pound. Two boats went through with it wrapped round the rudders. The Company's gone. The Commissioner's gone. The bunting's ours now. What does a Jubilee cost, after?

left.label: Pay the town to clear it
left.outcome: A day's wages for a day's bunting. The town keeps some. It flies from the inn for a year.

right.label: The bunting is the Company's problem
right.outcome: "The Company's gone. It's always gone, after."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Board has written. Eleven lines. It uses the word 'creditable', which is the Board's second-highest word. It uses my name twice and yours once. I have never been so happy with a letter. Shall we frame it?

text_variants.text: The Board has written. Three lines. It uses the word 'regrettable'. It uses your name three times and mine not at all, for which I am, Keeper, not grateful. What did you think the gauge would buy you?

left.label: Frame it
left.outcome: It hangs beside the other frames. There are many frames.

right.label: Give it to Quenn
right.outcome: He does, after a struggle. She puts it in the drawer with the survey.

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: It is off. The Jubilee. The Board has cancelled it 'pending review of the summit'. Twenty years, Keeper. I do not blame you. I have been trying for a week to blame you and I cannot.

left.label: Hold a town Jubilee instead
left.outcome: No Board, no band, no bunting from Ardent. The town does it anyway. Pell weeps and says it was magnificent.

right.label: There will be another year
right.outcome: "Will there." He does not make it a question.

cards.notes: Reached via delayed follow-up from ma04_15 or cri_company; the Jubilee can be cancelled by external events.
